Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS has introduced a new 20 GHz PSG XG7-class analog signal generator designed to improve measurement accuracy and increase testing capacity without requiring additional rack space. The instrument combines two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis for engineers working on advanced wireless, aerospace and defense, and high-speed digital applications.
Keysight's PSG XG7-class helps engineers achieve clearer measurements by reducing signal-source noise, offering low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise and a low broadband noise floor. Its dual-channel configuration enables more testing within the same rack space, while output power of up to +22 dBm helps maintain the required signal level, even with lossy cables and test fixtures.
The company's new generator provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset. Its broadband noise floor reaches -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. A hybrid architecture with software-based mode switching further enables the instrument to optimize performance for different testing requirements.
The platform also supports faster upgrades with Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments compatibility, familiar connections and settings similar to previous-generation equipment, allowing teams to reuse existing test procedures. The launch expands Keysight's test and measurement portfolio and helps engineers improve testing efficiency and advance device development.
How Are Competitors Advancing in the Testing Domain?
Keysight faces competition from Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV and Vistance Networks, Inc. VISN. Viavi is expanding its testing portfolio for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8. The company introduced an Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution to test high-speed AI data center networks. Viavi has launched the CyberFlood CF50 for application, security and AI workload testing at speeds of up to 100G.
Vistance continues to focus on testing and validation for advanced broadband network technologies. Its Aurora Networks business provides services for integration, user experience and performance testing of network solutions. Vistance has expanded its DOCSIS and PON offerings, including DOCSIS 4.0 and 50G PON technologies, to support network testing, validation and modernization for broadband operators.

Keysight's shares have rallied 108.3% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 96.0%.

KEYSIGHT TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
Keysight Technologies, Inc. announced the new 20 gigahertz (GHz) PSG XG7-class analog signal generator, combining two fully independent channels in a single chassis measuring two rack units (2U). Its exceptional low noise and calibrated output power help engineers evaluate device performance more clearly, while the compact dual-channel design increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space. Keysight?s new dual channel analog signal generator increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space.
Across demanding test environments, such as in aerospace and defense, advanced wireless, and high-speed digital applications, noise from the signal source can mask the behavior engineers need to measure. Engineering teams must also increase test capacity while managing limited rack space and avoiding costly changes to established test systems. The new PSG addresses these requirements with low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise, a low broadband noise floor, calibrated output power and two independent channels in a compact chassis. Key benefits of the new XG7-class include: Enhanced measurement visibility: Ultra-low noise helps engineers evaluate device performance without the signal source masking critical behavior.
Expanded test capacity: Two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis enable teams to run more tests without increasing rack space. Improved performance in lossy test setups: Clean, calibrated output power up to +22 decibel-milliwatt (dBm) helps maintain the required signal level at the device under test, including through lossy cables and test fixtures. Faster technology refresh: Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments (SCPI) compatibility, familiar rear-panel connections and settings aligned with previous-generation instruments help teams reuse existing automation and test procedures.
The PSG provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz, measured at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset, together with a broadband noise floor of -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. Its hybrid architecture uses software mode switching to optimize performance across different applications, while calibrated output power up to +22 dBm helps compensate for losses in cables and test fixtures.

Keysight Technologies, Inc. stock (ISIN US49338L1035) is trading firmly supported by a recent earnings beat, after the company reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 3.07 for its fiscal Q3 2026 versus Wall Street expectations of USD 2.46 and revenue of USD 1.9 billion, as highlighted on September 16, 2026.
Q3 2026 results and Q4 guidance in focus
According to Barchart on September 16, 2026, Keysight reported fiscal Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of USD 3.07, clearly above the USD 2.46 consensus estimate, and revenue of USD 1.9 billion for the quarter.
As Barchart reports, the company guided for fiscal Q4 2026 adjusted EPS between USD 3.34 and USD 3.40 and revenue in a range of USD 1.9 billion to USD 2.0 billion, signaling continued earnings growth compared with the Q3 2026 EPS level of USD 3.07 and similar revenue magnitude.
Order momentum and backlog support the investment case
Keysight’s recent performance is closely tied to strong demand from artificial intelligence and high-performance computing customers. As Yahoo Finance reported on September 16, 2026, Keysight recorded a 56 percent jump in orders in its latest reported quarter and finished the period with a record backlog, providing visibility for scheduled shipments into fiscal Q4 2026.
Management’s Q4 2026 revenue guidance of USD 1.930 billion to USD 1.950 billion cited by Yahoo Finance indicates that, at the midpoint, revenue would modestly exceed the Q3 2026 level of USD 1.9 billion and align with the broader Q4 range reported by Barchart, underscoring stable top-line expectations into the fiscal year end.
Order strength and backlog are particularly relevant for investors because they help support Keysight’s ability to convert demand into revenue and earnings over the coming quarters. The combination of a 56 percent order increase and record backlog, together with Q4 2026 guidance slightly above the Q3 revenue baseline, suggests that the company’s exposure to AI-related test and measurement equipment is now a central driver of its near-term financial trajectory.
Analyst sentiment and valuation backdrop
Beyond reported figures, analyst sentiment on Keysight Technologies stock remains constructive. As Barchart notes in its September 16, 2026 overview, the stock carries a consensus Strong Buy rating from 12 Wall Street analysts, with a mean price target of USD 418.42 that implies around 33.5 percent potential upside from the then-current share price level.
According to Yahoo Finance on September 16, 2026, Keysight shares had fallen 11.1 percent over the prior three months despite an 82.1 percent gain over the past year, and the stock currently holds a Zacks Rank 1, which Zacks characterizes as Strong Buy.
The juxtaposition of a double-digit three-month decline with an 82.1 percent twelve-month gain, alongside a Strong Buy consensus and a price target more than one-third above the prevailing price, illustrates a setup in which recent volatility coexists with positive earnings revisions and supportive long-term demand trends. For investors, this contrast between short-term price weakness and strong fundamental and analyst signals is an important part of the Keysight Technologies stock story.
Despite strong demand and a supportive rating backdrop, several risks remain visible. As Yahoo Finance points out, Keysight still faces policy exposure, supply constraints and a lower recurring-revenue mix, which together keep the investment case from being entirely one-sided even with accelerating orders and revenue.
Execution risk is also evident in order timing and supply chain management. According to Zacks on September 16, 2026, the next-quarter earnings estimate for Keysight has risen 27.7 percent over the past month, while management aims to realize 80 to 90 percent of a USD 100 million cost-synergy target on a run-rate basis exiting fiscal 2026, but valuation and timing risks related to policy and supply remain part of the picture.
This mix of strong earnings revision momentum and ongoing execution and policy risk means that, while Keysight’s near-term outlook is supported by rapidly growing orders and an expanding backlog, investors still need to weigh potential volatility around supply, customer mix and macro policy developments when assessing the Keysight Technologies stock.
Keysight Technologies stock price context
Keysight Technologies stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker KEYS and trades in USD; recent price data around mid-September 2026 show the shares moving in response to the Q3 2026 earnings release on August 18, 2026, when, as Barchart reports, the stock fell 5.6 percent on the day despite beating earnings expectations.
For investors following Keysight Technologies stock into the coming quarters, the key numerical checkpoints are the Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of USD 3.07 versus USD 2.46 consensus, Q3 revenue of USD 1.9 billion, Q4 2026 guidance for EPS between USD 3.34 and USD 3.40 and revenue of USD 1.9 to USD 2.0 billion, the 56 percent order growth and record backlog, and the analyst consensus Strong Buy rating with a mean price target of USD 418.42, all as of mid-September 2026.

Keysight Enables UC Berkeley Research to Advance 6G Over-the-Air Testing
Keysight helps move innovative OTA measurement techniques toward practical application for emerging 6G devices and systems
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced a new collaboration supporting research at the Berkeley Wireless Research Center (BWRC) that aims to accelerate and improve testing of next-generation wireless devices. Led by Professor Aditya Muppala at the University of California, Berkeley, the research explores a new approach to over-the-air (OTA) testing designed to help engineers better evaluate the performance of increasingly complex 6G devices and systems.
The wireless industry is exploring upper-midband spectrum, often referred to as FR3, as part of the path toward 6G. As devices employ increasingly complex antenna and beamforming architectures, engineers need faster and more flexible ways to characterize how systems transmit and receive energy across three-dimensional space. These challenges are also relevant to advanced radar and non-terrestrial network (NTN) applications.
Professor Muppala's research will explore new ways to measure radiated performance that could reduce the time and complexity involved in testing advanced wireless systems. By enabling faster, highly accurate measurements and greater flexibility across different frequency bands, the approach has the potential to help engineers evaluate next-generation devices more efficiently, accelerating their path from research to real-world deployment.
Aditya Muppala, Assistant Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, said: "I'm excited to have Keysight behind this research as we explore new approaches to over-the-air antenna measurement. We believe these techniques have the potential to be a game changer for how OTA systems are deployed in real-world environments, making advanced measurements faster, more flexible, and more practical for emerging wireless systems."
Giampaolo Tardioli, Vice President and General Manager at Keysight, said: "Keysight is excited to work with BWRC to advance innovative approaches to wireless testing. By bringing together BWRC's pioneering research with Keysight's test expertise and real-world OTA chamber capabilities, we believe this work can lead to important breakthroughs and help accelerate industry adoption of faster, more flexible measurement techniques for 6G."

The Commercial Communications business was the biggest contributor to CSG's growth. Revenues reached $1.006 billion, up 56% year over year, marking its first billion-dollar quarter. The trend reflects increasing testing requirements in high-speed connectivity and AI data-center infrastructure.

The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) timeline now targets the first 6G standard for March 2029, and management said customers are moving from exploratory research into funded development programs. Demand was driven by advanced radar architectures, autonomous platforms, satellite systems and resilient positioning, navigation and timing solutions. Memory, auto and industrial, IST, Product Test and Robotics are expected to grow sequentially in the second half.

Can Keysight's Advanced Testing Generator Boost Its Growth Prospects?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:40 AM PDT 3 min read
Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS has introduced a new 20 GHz PSG XG7-class analog signal generator designed to improve measurement accuracy and increase testing capacity without requiring additional rack space. The instrument combines two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis for engineers working on advanced wireless, aerospace and defense, and high-speed digital applications.
Keysight's PSG XG7-class helps engineers achieve clearer measurements by reducing signal-source noise, offering low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise and a low broadband noise floor. Its dual-channel configuration enables more testing within the same rack space, while output power of up to +22 dBm helps maintain the required signal level, even with lossy cables and test fixtures.
The company's new generator provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset. Its broadband noise floor reaches -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. A hybrid architecture with software-based mode switching further enables the instrument to optimize performance for different testing requirements.
The platform also supports faster upgrades with Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments compatibility, familiar connections and settings similar to previous-generation equipment, allowing teams to reuse existing test procedures. The launch expands Keysight's test and measurement portfolio and helps engineers improve testing efficiency and advance device development.
How Are Competitors Advancing in the Testing Domain?
Keysight faces competition from Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV and Vistance Networks, Inc. VISN. Viavi is expanding its testing portfolio for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8. The company introduced an Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution to test high-speed AI data center networks. Viavi has launched the CyberFlood CF50 for application, security and AI workload testing at speeds of up to 100G.
Vistance continues to focus on testing and validation for advanced broadband network technologies. Its Aurora Networks business provides services for integration, user experience and performance testing of network solutions. Vistance has expanded its DOCSIS and PON offerings, including DOCSIS 4.0 and 50G PON technologies, to support network testing, validation and modernization for broadband operators.

Keysight's shares have rallied 108.3% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 96.0%.
Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 26.05 forward earnings, lower than 28.03 for the industry.
Earnings estimates for 2026 have risen 12.6% to $11.45 per share over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have increased 18.1% to $14.07.

Keysight Enables UC Berkeley Research to Advance 6G Over-the-Air Testing
Keysight helps move innovative OTA measurement techniques toward practical application for emerging 6G devices and systems
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced a new collaboration supporting research at the Berkeley Wireless Research Center (BWRC) that aims to accelerate and improve testing of next-generation wireless devices. Led by Professor Aditya Muppala at the University of California, Berkeley, the research explores a new approach to over-the-air (OTA) testing designed to help engineers better evaluate the performance of increasingly complex 6G devices and systems.
The wireless industry is exploring upper-midband spectrum, often referred to as FR3, as part of the path toward 6G. As devices employ increasingly complex antenna and beamforming architectures, engineers need faster and more flexible ways to characterize how systems transmit and receive energy across three-dimensional space. These challenges are also relevant to advanced radar and non-terrestrial network (NTN) applications.
Professor Muppala's research will explore new ways to measure radiated performance that could reduce the time and complexity involved in testing advanced wireless systems. By enabling faster, highly accurate measurements and greater flexibility across different frequency bands, the approach has the potential to help engineers evaluate next-generation devices more efficiently, accelerating their path from research to real-world deployment.
Aditya Muppala, Assistant Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, said: "I'm excited to have Keysight behind this research as we explore new approaches to over-the-air antenna measurement. We believe these techniques have the potential to be a game changer for how OTA systems are deployed in real-world environments, making advanced measurements faster, more flexible, and more practical for emerging wireless systems."
Giampaolo Tardioli, Vice President and General Manager at Keysight, said: "Keysight is excited to work with BWRC to advance innovative approaches to wireless testing. By bringing together BWRC's pioneering research with Keysight's test expertise and real-world OTA chamber capabilities, we believe this work can lead to important breakthroughs and help accelerate industry adoption of faster, more flexible measurement techniques for 6G."
